So first off there's a lot of good and it's promising, but a few things that weren't immediately clear that are great parts of the game. You can cut projectiles. You can dash cancel any part of your attack. You have invincibility during the beginning of your dash. You have money farms available from the start to hit in the hub between runs for more currency for upgrades. There are stations that you can upgrade with boss materials. Now for what I hate. Bosses summon side enemies depending on how much damage they've taken during the fight, I have been at a massive disadvantage from dealing too much damage due to this than is needed and the second boss has an incredibly awful and quick thorns attack that can be used back to back with no down time. The cover art when my friend looked at it, thought it was AI at first even though it isn't. maybe it's the side tones in the hair that alarmed his brain. The third attack for the axe is very slow to start up and getting down the timing of attacks in general which is a big part of the game takes a dozen runs. Not bad, seems promising.

[h2] 《Hollow Survivors》 [/h2] [h3] 动作肉鸽？类幸存者？不伦不类！[/h3] 游戏的《哈迪斯》味儿太重了，例如天赋系统，闪电系天赋[spoiler]（宙斯） [/spoiler]、反弹系天赋[spoiler]（雅典娜）[/spoiler]、复仇系天赋[spoiler]（阿瑞斯）[/spoiler]。又例如战斗系统，依靠闪避躲开敌人的攻击后跟进打出连段，附带一个通用的远程输出手段。 但问题是你游戏的战斗逻辑完全不对呀！在《哈迪斯》里，主角的生命值是一个[u]数值[/u]，可以通过局内战利品强化增长的，可以通过一定关卡后得到回复的，最重要的是接触怪物这个动作本身不会受到损伤生命值，只有受到怪物的攻击动作后才会受到损伤。 而在《Hollow Survivors》里，主角的生命值是一个[u]数量[/u]，无法局内增长，也无法击杀boss后回复，[i]只要接触到怪物就会收到损伤！[/i]碰撞伤害这一个点会直接让整个游戏的战斗逻辑发生变化，因为玩家不可以再肆意闪避，否则会有直接撞到怪物而遭受损伤的风险。 因此在这种战斗逻辑的环境下，玩家采取的行动模式一般都是克制的，必须要等到怪物攻击后确定了位置再冲上去打输出，这样才能避免冲上去撞掉血的尴尬情形，玩起来简直像是个音乐游戏。主角低下的性能、初始微弱的攻防数值、怪物无受击硬直、几乎为零的回复手段...都像一道道枷锁禁锢着玩家，让玩家操作起来要步步谨慎，尽量预留更多数量的血来应对Boss战。 然而，这个游戏似乎忘记了它是一个[u]“类幸存者”[/u]游戏，那这比《哈迪斯》更硬核的战斗，更大量的局外成长，更微小的局内成长[strike] （甚至同类型的天赋效果还会递减，也就是越打越弱）[/strike]，更耐揍的怪物，空间有限的Boss房间......以上种种都在折磨玩家，仿佛告诉玩家，我就是没打算让你爽。 因此希望制作组搞清楚，这个游戏究竟要做成硬核战斗的动作肉鸽，还是爽爽刷怪的类幸存者？[u]目前来看，“战斗&爽！”并未成功。[/u] [code] 关注我们[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ikun-GameCollector]小黑子集游社 [/url]， 以获得更多游戏测评推荐 [/code] [b]游戏综合评分：（5.75/10）[/b] [list] [*]画面&音乐（10/10） 画面非常好看的像素风，不论是游戏封面还是角色，都很精美[strike] （凭这一点就够我给你好评）[/strike]。但你能不能把标题画面的那张图也换成像素的？跟游戏封面一样也行啊，标题画面的图不好看之余，还格格不入的；游戏的音乐还可以，打击音效很过瘾。 [*]创意&玩法（4/10） 动作肉鸽+类幸存者，想法很好，但未做好。 [*]手感&难度（5/10） 游戏打击手感不错；游戏局外成长太多，局内天赋太弱，没有回复手段让游戏的难度很高。 [*]丰富&耐玩（4/10） 武器有四种，但都没有衍生技，也就是只能平A；局内天赋种类太少且缺乏创新。 [/list]

"Hollow Survivors: Prologue" is isn't a game at all, it's just an ad for [i]Hollow Survivors[/i]. Talk about store pollution... Misleading marketing like this is an abuse of the Steam storefront and the "free" category. The product this is advertising, [i]Hollow Survivors: Prologue[/i] is a garbage ripoff of Vampire Survivors (copyright Poncle, 2021) where the developer seeks to basically rip off someone else's entire game and get paid for someone else's work.... but that's not really relevant, because this isn't Hollow Survivors, it's just an advert for it! Incorrectly published adverts are harmful.. they take up visibility that should instead be afforded to ethical developers who do the right thing. And it makes it harder for us to find those ethically made games. Valve provides a specific way to handle demos, free trials and advertisments. It is clearly outlined in the [url=https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/application/demos]Steamworks Documentation for creating Demos[/url]... something I would say is mandatory reading before anyone thinks about abusing Steam Direct. This "developer" either didn't responsibly try to understand Steam, or worse, deliberately and wilfully chose to ignore the correct process just to pollute Steam with for-profit advertising. Either way, this is unprofessional and bad for gamers, and here we are, looking at an advert. The purpose of this advertisement is to get you to pay $10 for pixelcrap, that's how much the full game costs. Abusing Steam to advertise garbage is really never okay, especially because, as mentioned, there's a correct process to follow and the developer chose to do the wrong thing, instead. Now onto pricing and value. As an advertisement, this is only free in the same way that adverts on Youtube and banner ads in your browser are. This is a game demo that's been dumped on Steam to advertise another Steam store page in the hopes of raking in some cash. Just because advertisements are free, doesn't mean they're worth your time. It's important to understand there's a formal process to create a demo/page for a game which hasn't been followed here: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/application/demos While it might seem like an innocuous mistake, publishing demos and advertisements as if they are full games is misleading and in some ways harmful. This advertisement is taking up marketing space and visibility that would be better made available to a developer that's done the right thing and created a full game. Instead, that visibility is given over to a demo/advert that's been published incorrectly and is polluting the marketplace. It's unclear if this mistake was made through incompetence or a deliberate intent to mislead gamers. Often developers may choose to incorrectly publish demo/advertisements as separate games as a cheap way to bypass paying Valve for marketing presence on the Steam front page, which may seem clever to them, but it's harmful behaviour and it's not good for gamers. Advertisements and incorrectly published demos don't add +1 to your game collector count, they aren't full games. It's impossible for me to recommend this incorrectly published advertising spam to gamers, you deserve better than adverts. There are over 140,000 games on Steam, not every one of them is a hidden gem. I'm here to help gamers find the ones that actually matter in that sea of Steam Direct self-published mess. If you don't agree with my findings in this review, you should definitely download it and play it to see for yourself. I'm happy to have helped you make an informed choice, regardless of the outcome.

Hollow Survivors: Prologue, created by Danny Deer, is a compact but engaging entry into the increasingly crowded survivor-like genre, offering a focused experience that emphasizes momentum, build experimentation, and steady progression. Even as a prologue, it manages to capture the addictive loop that defines this style of game: start weak, fight through escalating waves, accumulate power, and push your limits a little further with each run. It does not attempt to reinvent the formula, but it executes it with enough confidence and polish to stand on its own as a worthwhile experience. The gameplay revolves around navigating confined arenas while facing continuous enemy swarms that grow denser and more aggressive over time. Movement and positioning are crucial, as survival depends on your ability to weave through incoming threats while maximizing your offensive output. Combat feels responsive and immediate, with attacks and abilities triggering quickly and clearly, allowing players to stay focused on the flow of the action. As the run progresses, the screen fills with enemies, projectiles, and visual effects, creating a sense of controlled chaos that is both demanding and satisfying. The transition from fragile beginnings to overwhelming strength is handled well, making each successful run feel like a carefully built momentum rather than a random outcome. A major strength of the game lies in its upgrade and build system. Throughout each run, players are offered a variety of enhancements that can significantly alter how their character performs. Some upgrades focus on raw damage or attack speed, while others introduce new mechanics or synergize with existing abilities. This encourages a flexible approach, where players adapt to the options presented rather than relying on a single predetermined strategy. The system rewards experimentation, and discovering combinations that complement each other can lead to powerful, sometimes unexpected results. This sense of discovery is a key part of the game’s appeal, giving each run a slightly different flavor even within the prologue’s limited content. Complementing the run-based structure is a layer of meta-progression that provides long-term motivation. Resources collected during gameplay can be used to unlock permanent upgrades or improvements, ensuring that even failed attempts contribute to future success. This progression system helps smooth out the difficulty curve and keeps players invested, as there is always a sense that you are gradually becoming stronger or more capable. It also reinforces the loop of repeated runs, making the game easy to return to even after setbacks. The atmosphere adds another dimension to the experience, with a dark, slightly melancholic tone that sets it apart from more brightly styled entries in the genre. The pixel-art visuals are clean and readable, which is essential given the density of on-screen action, but they also carry a sense of mood that supports the game’s setting. Character designs and enemy types are distinct enough to remain recognizable even in chaotic moments, and the environments, while not overly detailed, provide a consistent backdrop for the action. Sound design complements this with functional effects and a subdued soundtrack that enhances the tension without becoming distracting. However, the limitations of the prologue become increasingly noticeable over extended play. The variety of enemies, upgrades, and environments is relatively small, which can lead to a sense of repetition once you have explored the available combinations. While the core loop remains satisfying, the lack of additional systems or surprises means that the experience can plateau sooner than in more fully developed titles. There is also a degree of unevenness in the difficulty curve, with certain spikes that may feel abrupt, particularly for players still learning the mechanics. Despite these constraints, Hollow Survivors: Prologue succeeds in delivering a polished and engaging slice of what could become a much larger and more complex game. Its strengths lie in the fluidity of its combat, the flexibility of its build system, and the steady sense of progression that encourages repeated play. It is easy to pick up, satisfying to master in short sessions, and effective at showcasing its core ideas without unnecessary complexity. In its current form, it stands as a strong proof of concept that demonstrates a clear understanding of the genre’s appeal. While it lacks the depth and variety needed for long-term staying power, it provides enough substance to be enjoyable on its own and leaves a positive impression of what the full version might achieve with expanded content and refinement. Rating: 7/10
